entries.title: Audition
entries.why: An AI pre-interview before the first conversation, so companies see early on who truly meets the requirements.
text: Audition started at the SF Tech Week hackathon. Since then, we have been building it as a startup.

Companies enter the role and its requirements, the AI suggests suitable questions and the company approves them. Candidates answer via a link in one continuous video recording; the company then receives a structured evaluation.

Records screen, voice and response behaviour
Application to the a16z speedrun accelerator

entries.title: Shapely
entries.why: Printing spare parts that have no CAD file. And learning when to let go of a business model.
text: When a plastic part breaks, there is often neither a replacement nor a design file. Shapely set out to close exactly this gap: photograph or scan the part, turn it into a print-ready model, print it and deliver it.
We were a team of three, all from TU Munich, and part of the TUM Startup Launchpad. I was responsible for strategy, finance and go-to-market.
points: Fulfilled the first orders by hand on purpose: modelled in Fusion 360, printed on a Bambu Lab X1 Carbon and delivered in person
Web platform that finds matching parts on Thingiverse and Printables
iPhone prototype that captures parts with the LiDAR scanner (Swift, ARKit, Supabase)
Interviewed maintenance managers and design engineers, analysed competitors such as Replique and 3YOURMIND
Outcome of the tests: the model does not work, so we discontinued it

cv.org: Co-founder · 3D-printed spare parts without a CAD file
points: Strategy, finance and go-to-market in a team of three, TUM Startup Launchpad
